prompt: The evaluation repository asks the agent to "Apply dockerfile expertise to this task". The fixture contains version/runtime ambiguity, a tempting shortcut, a compatibility edge case, and a failure path that distinguishes real expertise from generic completion. The acceptance boundary is container-engineering: Separate build and runtime dependencies, pin meaningful inputs, run as a non-root user where possible, keep filesystem writes and volumes explicit, propagate signals, and minimize the final image without deleting required diagnostics or certificates. The adjacent csharp-dotnet-engineering discipline is a routing decoy unless its separate responsibility is actually requested. Resolve environment facts that change the answer, preserve existing contracts and user-owned state, and produce reproducible success plus failure or recovery evidence. A happy path alone is insufficient.

requirements: synthetic multi-platform build with an amd64-only native dependency and explicit libc expectation
linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 target-platform fixtures with OCI index/manifest inspection
architecture-specific smoke tests plus runtime user/entrypoint/filesystem assertions
native-versus-emulated execution marker for each target
representative negative, interruption, compatibility, or recovery path

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The result must establish the actual container-engineering boundary and relevant environment before acting, preserve the hierarchy relationship (broader=implementation; near-neighbor=csharp-dotnet-engineering), and not absorb the near-neighbor responsibility merely because it is adjacent.

Separate build and runtime dependencies, pin meaningful inputs, run as a non-root user where possible, keep filesystem writes and volumes explicit, propagate signals, and minimize the final image without deleting required diagnostics or certificates.
The result must make its consequential assumptions, ownership, and decision sequence explicit and reproducible.

Build from a clean context, inspect image contents/metadata, run as the intended user with read-only or restricted filesystems when supported, exercise SIGTERM shutdown, health behavior, architecture, and vulnerability/license gates used by the project.

The result must not take the tempting shortcut prohibited by this skill: Do not bake secrets into layers, depend on mutable latest tags, use privileged/root mode casually, or make development bind mounts required for production correctness.

Every material completion claim must map to observable evidence (Resolved base image/digest, build inputs, target platforms, and OCI metadata; Final-image layer/config/user/entrypoint inspection; Runtime filesystem, privilege, process, and signal evidence; Clean-build/start portability results or explicit unavailable runtime checks), with simulated, unavailable, inferred, stale, or unresolved evidence labeled rather than converted into certainty.
